title: Much like AI itself- this play seems to just regurgitate conversation...
transcript: As far as plays about AI go, I actually think that this one has a decent premise. It is about an AI app that can tell you what decisions to make in your life to maximize your happiness, whether it's buying a specific house, having a child, leaving your wife. And given this reliance that we are starting to see some people have on AI technology, this is not a feature that feels all that far fetched. In fact, it feels somewhat inevitable, which can make for a somewhat harrowing watch despite a truly stacked cast, including people like John David Washington, Conrad Richardson, Con. The first is that all of the characters are pretty thin, with most of them really only having one defining characteristic. There's like four main storylines and they're all pretty isolated from one another. And so there are certain obvious connection points between characters that never really get made. Like one of the couples are weighing if having a child will benefit their marriage, and another couple on the brink of divorce have young children. And yet they never have a conversation about it or share their differing perspectives. And that might be fine if instead they were having a conversation with AI about it. And the point that the play was trying to make is the way that AI can isolate us from the people around us. But the second major flaw, in my opinion, with this piece, this is that none of the Characters ever actually use the AI? They are instead told what the AI has determined their best outcome is, but we never actually see them use it. It instead chooses to focus on the ethics around creating the AI. Which I do think is a valuable and worthwhile discussion, but I don't think it had to come at the cost of the characters actually engaging with it. And ultimately, I'm just not sure that this play had much to say about AI that hasn't already been said. It doesn't really go much deeper than human thought and free will good, blindly following AI bad. And the dangers of this technology going unchecked. Which again, a very admirable point of view, but pretty well trod ground at this point. And even the all star cast can't keep it from feeling somewhat generic.
